claims.summary: Over every field, let H be a nonempty h-element subset of {0,...,L-1} and u>=0 with min(H)>=u+h+1. For formal nodes a0=0,a1,...,a_(L-1), evaluate the L+1 monomials with exponents ({0,...,L-1}\H) union {L+u,...,L+u+h}. Their maximal minors divided by the full Vandermonde are polynomials with gcd1. Applies to the supported quinary nine-node and ternary seven-node degree-one input blocks, without asserting primitive combined boundary cofactors.
claims.assessment: Working all-characteristic proof: monic remainder unit elimination leaves an h by(h+1) matrix whose ordinary linear part is a shifted coefficient matrix. A polynomial-shift incidence argument gives codimension at least2; weighted homogeneity excludes any common divisor in the nonlinear minors. Finite-free splitting transfers this to the anchored root ring. Positive and negative controls are exact symbolic identities.
claims.rationale: A characteristic-free criterion for primitive normalized sparse interpolation minors, actually applied to a source block in the boundary transfer. Potential reusable interest beyond the current case; no external novelty audit performed. It does not settle the joint weighted transfer or another threshold.
claims.next_action: Keep the full coupled transfer separate; compare this criterion with generalized Vandermonde and Schur-minor literature before any novelty or publication claim.

relationships: Reuse and explicitly reprove the characteristic-free monic splitting/freeness argument; the new lemma also permits characteristic2, unlike the full square-root descent statement.
The application is to the sparse degree-one input minors in the complete Cauchy-Binet transfer; this does not assert primitivity of the coupled leading vector.
The ternary first-support zero row survives despite the new primitive-input conclusion, serving as a scope control.
